content: This product may contain inactive ingredients that could potentially trigger allergic reactions or other complications. Liquid, powdered, or other forms of this product might include sugar and/or aspartame. Liquid formulations may also contain alcohol. Exercise caution if you have conditions such as diabetes, alcohol dependence, liver disease, or phenylketonuria (PKU), or if you are required to limit or avoid these substances in your diet. During pregnancy, this product should only be used if absolutely necessary. It is not known whether this product passes into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Maintain a comprehensive list of all products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Magnesium can bind with certain medications, reducing their absorption. If you are taking a tetracycline-type medication (e.g., demeclocycline, doxycycline, minocycline, tetracycline), ensure a gap of at least 2 to 3 hours between the doses of the magnesium supplement and the medication. Check the labels of all your prescription and non-prescription/herbal products (e.g., antacids, laxatives, vitamins) as they may contain magnesium. In the event of an overdose with severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., magnesium blood levels, kidney function) should be conducted while you are taking this medication. Attend all medical and laboratory appointments as scheduled. Magnesium supplements are available in various forms and concentrations, many of which can be obtained without a prescription. Maintain a well-balanced diet. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this product at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. This medication is a mineral supplement used to prevent and treat low magnesium levels in the blood. Certain brands are also used to alleviate symptoms of excessive stomach acid, such as stomach upset, heartburn, and acid indigestion. Magnesium is essential for the normal functioning of cells, nerves, muscles, bones, and the heart. A well-balanced diet typically provides adequate magnesium levels, but certain conditions may cause the body to lose magnesium faster than it can be replenished through diet. Take this product orally as directed. Follow all instructions on the product packaging. Each dose should be taken with a full glass of water (8 ounces or 240 milliliters) unless otherwise directed by your doctor. Swallow extended-release capsules and delayed-release/enteric-coated tablets or capsules whole. Do not crush or chew these forms, as doing so can release the drug all at once, increasing the risk of side effects. Do not split extended-release tablets unless they have a score line and your doctor or pharmacist advises you to do so. If using a liquid product, use a medication measuring device to ensure accurate dosing. Avoid using a household spoon, as it may not provide the correct dose. Take this medication regularly to maximize its benefits. Try to take it at the same time(s) each day. Dosage is based on your medical condition and response to treatment. Do not increase your dose or take it more frequently than directed on the product packaging or by your doctor. Inform your doctor if symptoms of low magnesium levels (e.g., muscle cramps, fatigue, irritability, depression) persist or worsen. Stomach upset and diarrhea may occur. Taking this product with a meal can help reduce these effects. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, remember that they have determined the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking a magnesium supplement, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues.
